title: DeepMind's AI Agents Find Two Weak Spots in 1024-Bit RSA
dek: Modern 2048-bit keys stay safe, but AI is speeding up codebreaking research.

facts.label: Lower cost per extra 1024-bit key cracked
Less CPU time in signature forgery demo

caption:
Encryption breakthroughs used to take years. Google DeepMind's AI agents did it in weeks. 🔐

Guided by human cryptographers, DeepMind's AI agents found two new weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA. One shows that signature padding offers no extra protection once an attacker controls about half the signed block. The other is a new batch factoring algorithm that cuts the average cost of cracking each additional 1024-bit key by about 30x.

The good news: modern 2048-bit RSA keys used by banks, websites and messaging apps are not affected. The bigger story is speed. AI can now stress-test the math behind internet security far faster than before, so treating hardness as a fixed fact is getting risky.

We're tracking how AI is reshaping cybersecurity every day at AI Parabellum. If you still run old 1024-bit keys in servers, VPNs or code signing, this is your sign to upgrade.
